question.problem:
Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, approximate the probability that a fair spinner with five regions: red, green, orange, white, and blue, lands on green or white more than $25$ but less than $35$ times out of $80$ spins. Give your final answer to three decimal places. *Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$$\,0.09\,$
$\,-1.5\,$ $\,0.0582\,$ $\,0.0570\,$ $\,0.0559\,$
$\,-1.4\,$ $\,0.0708\,$ $\,0.0694\,$ $\,0.0681\,$
$\,-1.3\,$ $\,0.0854\,$ $\,0.0838\,$ $\,0.0823\,$
$z$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$$\,0.09\,$
$\,0.4\,$ $\,0.6808\,$ $\,0.6844\,$ $\,0.6879\,$
$\,0.5\,$ $\,0.7157\,$ $\,0.7190\,$ $\,0.7224\,$
$\,0.6\,$ $\,0.7486\,$ $\,0.7518\,$ $\,0.7549\,$
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=80$ and $p=0.4.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =80\cdot 0.4 \\  & =32 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =80\cdot (1-0.4) \\  & =48 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(80)(0.4)=32
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(80)(0.4)(1-0.4)=19.2.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(32,19.2).$

Now, we can estimate the desired probability $P(25<X<35).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(25<X<35)=P(26\le X\le 34)≈P(25.5\le Y\le 34.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(25.5\le Y\le 34.5) & =P(\frac{25.5-32}{\sqrt{19.2}}\le Z\le \frac{34.5-32}{\sqrt{19.2}}) \\  & ≈P(-1.48\le Z\le 0.57) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.57)-P(Z<-1.48) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.57)-P(Z\le -1.48) \\  & =Φ(0.57)-Φ(-1.48) \\  & =0.7157-0.0694 \\  & =0.6463\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(25<X<35)≈0.646.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of
$0.65.$
